cleanIntro:
This guide follows Savage Arms' Revel Lever Action manual (908035 Rev 1), which does not name the Revel Tactical, so check your variant against it. Savage prints one manual for its Revel lever actions and it never uses the word "Tactical". Every step below is quoted from that book and stated as generally as the book states it.

The Revel is a takedown rimfire with a tubular magazine. Two captive takedown pins in the receiver cover let the rifle come apart into upper and lower halves, and for cleaning the cover comes off with the bolt. Savage's own limit is plain: the bolt assembly and the trigger assembly are never taken apart.

steps.title: Know what you are holding
steps.action: This guide follows Savage Arms' Revel Lever Action manual (908035 Rev 1), which does not name the Revel Tactical, so check your variant against it. Every step below is quoted from that book and stated as generally as the book states it.
steps.prose: Savage's Revel book speaks of the Revel lever action as a whole and never prints the word Tactical. Its parts list names Classic and Heritage front sights and a receiver cover drilled with four scope base holes. If your rifle's receiver cover, sights or stock are not what the book shows, check how your rifle comes apart against the book before you start, and do not remove anything the book does not tell you to.
steps.quote: Revel lever action models are constructed with a tubular magazine.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 3: Basic Use, Loading, p.11

steps.title: Hammer half-cocked, safety on FULL SAFE
steps.action: Start with the hammer at HALF-COCKED and the safety button pressed fully to the right, FULL SAFE, with no red showing. Muzzle in a safe direction and your finger off the trigger for the whole of unloading.
steps.quote: Make sure the hammer is in the HALF-COCKED position and the manual safety is in the FULL SAFE position – FIGURE 13 & FIGURE 14.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 3: Basic Use, Unloading, p.14

steps.title: Safety to READY TO FIRE, lever opened
steps.action: With all your fingers inside the finger lever and none near the trigger, press the safety to READY TO FIRE (red band showing) and open the lever. That extracts and ejects any cartridge in the chamber.
steps.quote: With the utmost care to not touch the trigger, open the lever. This should extract and eject any cartridge that may be in the chamber.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 3: Basic Use, Unloading, step 1, p.15

steps.title: Lever left open, safety back to FULL SAFE, chamber checked
steps.action: Leave the lever open and press the safety back to FULL SAFE. Then look into the chamber and feel it, and confirm it is empty.
steps.quote: 2. Leaving the lever open, press the safety to the FULL SAFE position - FIGURE 13. Visibly and physically check to ensure that the chamber is clear of ammunition.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 3: Basic Use, Unloading, step 2, p.15

steps.title: Inner magazine tube out
steps.action: With the lever still open and your fingers out of the trigger guard, twist the end cap of the magazine tube counterclockwise and pull the inner tube out. Keep your hands away from the muzzle while you do it.
steps.quote: 3. With the lever remaining open and your fingers away from the trigger (and out of the trigger guard), unlock the inner magazine tube by twisting counterclockwise to open the end cap of the magazine tube and pull the inner tube out - FIGURE 15.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 3: Basic Use, Unloading, step 3, p.15
steps.warn: Be sure to keep your hands, fingers, and any other body parts away from the front of the muzzle during loading or unloading the magazine tube.

steps.title: Tilt and shake the magazine tube empty
steps.action: Hold a container ready to catch any rounds. Keeping the muzzle safe and your fingers away from the trigger, tilt the rifle downward and give it a good shake, then make sure the tube is empty and free of debris.
steps.quote: 4. Be prepared to catch any live rounds in a suitable container so they do not drop onto the ground. Keeping the firearm pointed in a safe direction and your fingers away from the trigger, tilt the firearm downward and give the firearm a good “shake”. This will help to ensure that no ammunition is housed in the magazine tube. Ensure the tube is empty, and free of debris.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 3: Basic Use, Unloading, step 4, p.15

steps.title: Lever closed, then worked several times
steps.action: Safety still on FULL SAFE, fingers inside the finger loop and away from the trigger: close the lever, then open and close it fully several times to be sure no unfired round is left in the rifle.
steps.quote: 6. With all of your fingers inside of the finger loop, fully open and close the lever several times to ensure that there is no unfired ammunition in the firearm.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 3: Basic Use, Unloading, step 6, p.15

steps.title: Top of the chamber and feed block checked
steps.action: Look at the top of the chamber and into the feed block and loading port, and make sure nothing is lodged there. Then check that the follower shows at the end of the inner tube and nothing is stuck inside it.
steps.quote: 7. Visibly check the top of the chamber and feed block/loading port to ensure that there is no ammunition lodged inside FIGURE 16.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 3: Basic Use, Unloading, step 7, p.15

steps.title: Inner tube back in, end cap locked
steps.action: Slide the inner tube back into the outer magazine tube until it seats fully, then twist the end cap clockwise to lock it.
steps.quote: 10. Re-insert the inner tube into the outer magazine tube. Once the inner magazine tube is seated fully, re-tighten the end cap by twisting clockwise - FIGURE 15.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 3: Basic Use, Unloading, step 10, p.16

steps.title: Lever worked again, chamber and feed checked again
steps.action: Move the safety to READY TO FIRE. With all your fingers in the finger loop and nothing near the trigger, open and close the lever several times, then inspect the chamber and the feed mechanism. Do this more than once. When you are certain the rifle is empty, close the lever, bring the hammer to HALF-COCKED and put the safety on FULL SAFE.
steps.quote: 13. Repeat steps 11 and 12 several times to confirm the chamber and magazine tube are clear of ammunition.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 3: Basic Use, Unloading, step 13, p.16

steps.title: Safety to READY TO FIRE, lever fully open
steps.action: Eye protection on. Muzzle in a safe direction, move the safety to READY TO FIRE and, with your fingers inside the finger loop and away from the trigger, open the finger lever fully. Check once more that the chamber, the magazine and the whole rifle are clear of ammunition.
steps.quote: 2. While keeping the firearm pointed in a safe direction, move the manual safety into the READY TO FIRE position. With all of your fingers inside the finger loop and away from the trigger, fully open the finger lever. Ensure that the chamber, magazine, and entire firearm is clear of ammunition.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 4: Maintenance, Takedown, step 2, p.19

steps.title: Safety back to FULL SAFE and kept there
steps.action: Put the safety on FULL SAFE. It stays there, with the lever open, for the whole of the takedown and reassembly. It is what stops the hammer snapping forward while the rifle is apart.
steps.quote: 3. Place the manual safety into the FULL SAFE position. Be sure to keep the lever open and the manual safety in the FULL SAFE position during disassembly and reassembly.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 4: Maintenance, Takedown, step 3, p.19
steps.warn: DO NOT MOVE THE MANUAL SAFETY TO OFF SAFE/READY TO FIRE WHEN THE TWO HALVES ARE SEPERATED. DO NOT ATTEMPT TO PRESS THE TRIGGER WHILE THE TWO HALVES ARE SEPERATED.

steps.title: Both takedown pins pressed out to the right
steps.action: With the lever fully open, press the two takedown pins in the cover toward the right until they stop. They are captive and do not come out of the cover, so do not force them further.
steps.quote: 4. With the lever fully open, locate and press in on the two takedown pins on the cover to the right until they come out as far as they will go. The takedown pins are captive and cannot be fully removed – FIGURE 25.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 4: Maintenance, Takedown, step 4, p.19

steps.title: Upper and lower halves pulled apart
steps.action: Pull the upper and lower halves in opposite directions to separate them. For transport or storage you stop here; for cleaning, carry on to the cover and bolt.
steps.aside: For transport or storing, stop disassembling at this point.
steps.quote: 5. Pull the lower and upper halves in the opposite directions. The firearm is now separated into upper and lower halves FIGURE 23 & FIGURE 24.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 4: Maintenance, Takedown, step 5, p.19

steps.title: Four cover screws out
steps.action: Unscrew the four hex screws on the receiver cover with a 5/64-inch hex wrench. Keep the screws together.
steps.quote: 3. To remove the cover for cleaning or maintenance, unscrew the four hex screws on the cover using a 5/64” hex wrench.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 4: Maintenance, Disassembly, step 3, p.21

steps.title: Cover lifted off with the bolt inside it
steps.action: Slide the cover carefully upward and off the barrel assembly. The bolt comes with it and slides forward freely inside the cover, so hold it in as you lift.
steps.quote: 4. The cover can now be removed with the bolt assembly. Carefully slide the cover upward and off of the barrel assembly. Be careful to retain the bolt within the cover as it will slide forward freely.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 4: Maintenance, Disassembly, step 4, p.21

steps.title: Bolt slid out of the front of the cover
steps.action: Slide the bolt out of the cover toward the front of the cover. Note which way the bolt face points, because it goes back in the same way.
steps.quote: 5. Carefully remove the bolt from the cover by sliding it out towards the front of the cover.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 4: Maintenance, Disassembly, step 5, p.21

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Upper and lower halves apart, cover off, bolt out. That is as far as Savage lets an owner go. Look through the bore from the breech end, never the muzzle, to be sure nothing is left in it.
steps.quote: DO NOT TAKE APART ANY OF THE BOLT ASSEMBLY. DO NOT DISASSEMBLE ANY FURTHER.
steps.cite: REVEL LEVER ACTION — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 4: Maintenance, Disassembly, p.21

deepAbsentReason: The book's disassembly ends on p.21 with the bolt out of the cover: 'DO NOT TAKE APART ANY OF THE BOLT ASSEMBLY. DO NOT DISASSEMBLE ANY FURTHER.' It forbids taking the trigger assembly apart in the same section ('Do not attempt to disassemble the TRIGGER ASSEMBLY.', p.21), and opens its maintenance section with 'Do not disassemble beyond what is recommended below.' (p.17). It publishes no deeper procedure.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: A small amount of powder solvent on the brush, then push the coated cleaning rod through the barrel several times
Swap the brush for a patch tip and push new patches through, several times
One patch saturated with firearm lubricant through the bore, then a dry patch to take off the excess
Shine a light down the barrel to check it is clear of obstructions and damage
Do not use the rifle if the barrel or chamber shows nicks, scratches, rust, pitting or other damage

cleaning.name: BOLT & RECEIVER
tasks: Wipe every bolt component clean of contaminants, then give it a very light coat of firearm lubricant; do not over-lubricate
Clean and lightly lubricate all interior metal surfaces
Inspect the trigger assembly for damage; if any part looks damaged or loose, do not use the rifle and contact Savage
Do not take apart the bolt assembly or the trigger assembly

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE TUBE
tasks: Remove the inner magazine tube and clean the inside of the outer tubular magazine
Check that the follower shows at the end of the inner tube and nothing is lodged inside it

reassembly: Bolt face pointing the same way as the cover, slide the bolt back into the front of the cover and rearward up to the notch on the bolt.

Lower the cover onto the upper half, holding the bolt in its original position; expect some spring tension as it seats. Pressing the forward takedown pin in can hold the cover on while you fit the screws.
Fit the four cover screws hand tight only, about 2-4 in-lbs, and do not over-tighten. If you pressed a takedown pin in, push it back out.
Check that the bolt still protrudes from the rear of the cover to the hammer cut-out.
To rejoin the halves: safety on FULL SAFE, hammer FULLY COCKED, finger lever fully open, and the bolt protruding from the rear of the upper half up to its notch.
Slide the lower half inside the upper half, watching the bolt and lever line up, then press both takedown pins back into the cover until they are flush on both sides.
fncheck: With no ammunition in the rifle and your fingers inside the finger loop and away from the trigger, open and close the lever several times and check that every part moves freely. Close the lever fully, move the safety to READY TO FIRE, carefully lower the hammer to HALF-COCKED and put the safety back on FULL SAFE. Cycle the action and work the safety several times; the bolt and lever must run smoothly and the safety must work in both positions. If anything binds or does not work, take it apart and start again, and if the problem stays, call Savage. If a scope is fitted to the cover, check its alignment.
